title: Biograd na Moru Prices and 2027 Budget Guide
metaDescription: Biograd na Moru costs for 2027: apartments, hotels, food, ferries and daily budgets, plus how prices have shifted and when to book for the best value.
content:
## How Biograd na Moru Prices Have Changed

Biograd na Moru sits on the Zadar Riviera, about 28 km southeast of Zadar. It has long been priced below Split, Dubrovnik and Hvar, but the gap has narrowed since Croatia adopted the euro in 2023. Rounding of prices at the changeover, wage growth in tourism and higher energy and food costs have pushed menu and rental prices up in steps rather than in one jump.

The most visible change is in accommodation. Hotels in the town now average roughly €85–105 a night for three stars and €125–155 for four stars, with five-star rooms near €290–310. Private apartments, which make up most of the town's beds, typically list at €70–120 for a studio or one-bedroom in peak season and €100–180 for two bedrooms.

Food has risen more gently. A casual pizza or sandwich lunch costs €5–15, and a sit-down dinner with a drink usually lands at €20–30 per person. Taxi fares and public transport remain modest, and the main ferry to Pašman is still cheap.

A sensible planning assumption for 2027 is a further rise of about 3–6% on 2026 prices, with the largest increases in July and August accommodation. Treat this as an estimate, not a published tariff.

## What Does a Realistic 2027 Budget Look Like?

### Budget traveller: €60–90 per person per day
This covers a hostel dorm bed (€25–40) or a basic private room (€50–70), self-catered breakfasts, a pizza or grill lunch, and local buses. Hostel options in Biograd are limited, so the budget range often means a basic room or a campsite (pitches from about €35).

### Mid-range couple: €110–170 per person per day
A 1–2 bedroom apartment near Bošana beach or the centre (€80–150 a night, split between two) plus restaurant dinners at €20–30 and one paid excursion per few days fits this band. In peak weeks, expect the top of the range.

### Comfort or family: €250+ per day for the household
Three- and four-star hotels with breakfast, or a three-bedroom apartment at €150–300+, sit here. A villa with a pool in the Kumenat or Crvena Luka areas runs €250–600+ a night, which becomes reasonable only when split between two or more families.

### Sample 7-night budget for two (peak season, 2027 estimate)
- Apartment: €560–840
- Food and drink: €350–550
- Local transport and ferry: €30–60
- Excursions (Kornati or Telašćica boat trip): €120–220
- Total: roughly €1,060–1,670

## Accommodation Prices by Type and Season

July and August are consistently the most expensive months, and rates can double compared with shoulder periods. May, June and September offer the best balance of warm sea and lower prices. A studio that costs €110 in August often drops to €60–75 in late May or mid-September.

Well-known hotels and resorts in town include Hotel Adriatic, Hotel Kornati, Hotel Ilirija, Hotel IN, Teatro Verdi Hotel and Crvena Luka Resort. Entry-level hotel rates in summer start around €95–120 per night, while the larger seafront properties go from about €190 to over €220 in high season.

The weakness of apartment hunting in Biograd is that the cheapest listings are often 1–2 km from the sea or on a main road. A studio at €60 looks good online, but a seafront or Bošana-area unit at €90 is usually the better deal once walking time and parking are counted.

## Food and Drink Costs

| Item | Typical price |
|---|---|
| Pizza or sandwich | €5–10 |
| Casual grill meal (ćevapi, pizza plate) | €10–18 |
| Restaurant main course | €15–30 |
| Three-course dinner for two, mid-range | €35–100 |

Seafood by weight is where bills climb. Fish priced per kilogram, ordered without checking the weight, is the usual reason a dinner for two passes €100. Ask for the price per kg and the approximate portion before ordering.

## Transport Costs

The Jadrolinija ferry on line 432 links Biograd with Tkon on the island of Pašman in about 15 minutes. The high-season adult one-way ticket is €3.50, with a low-season fare of €2.20. Children aged 3–12 pay €1.70 in high season. A vehicle with driver costs roughly €14.60 in high season. Departures run from early morning to late afternoon, with a gap of one to two hours between sailings.

Buses to Zadar cost about €4–6. Zadar Airport is the closest airport, roughly 20–25 minutes by car, and Biograd is also reachable from Split in about 1 hr 15 min by road.

## Money-Saving Tips for 2027

- **Book shoulder season.** Late May, June and September cut accommodation costs by 30–45% against August.
- **Stay one block back.** Apartments 300–500 m from the promenade cost noticeably less than waterfront ones, and the town is compact enough to walk everywhere.
- **Use the ferry for day trips.** A €3.50 crossing to Pašman is the cheapest way to get an island day, and cyclists pay about €3.30 per bike in high season.
- **Eat the big meal at lunch.** Many restaurants have fixed daily lunch plates well below dinner prices.
- **Self-cater breakfast.** Local supermarkets and the town market keep this near €3–5 per person.
- **Check the tourist tax.** Croatian tourist tax is charged per person per night on top of the rental price and varies by season; confirm whether it is included in the quoted rate.

## When to Book

For July and August 2027, apartments in the best locations are usually taken by early in the year. Booking by February to March secures the best selection and often lower rates. For June and September, booking four to eight weeks ahead is normally sufficient.

## FAQ

See the questions below for quick answers on cost, season and transport.

faq.question: How much does a week in Biograd na Moru cost in 2027?
faq.answer: A couple should plan roughly €1,060–1,670 for a peak-season week, covering an apartment, restaurant meals, local transport and one boat excursion. Budget travellers can lower this to about €420–630 per person with self-catering and shoulder-season dates.

faq.question: Is Biograd na Moru expensive compared with other Croatian destinations?
faq.answer: It is cheaper than Split, Dubrovnik and the Hvar area, though no longer a bargain. Apartments from about €70 a night and campsites from about €35 still give good value outside July and August.

faq.question: What is the cheapest time to visit Biograd na Moru?
faq.answer: Late May, June and September offer the lowest prices with swimmable sea. July and August are the peak, and accommodation prices can nearly double.

faq.question: How much is a meal in Biograd na Moru?
faq.answer: A pizza or sandwich costs €5–15, and a sit-down lunch €10–15. Dinner with a drink is usually €20–30 per person, and fish sold by weight can push it higher.

faq.question: How much is the ferry from Biograd to Pašman?
faq.answer: The Jadrolinija line 432 ferry to Tkon takes about 15 minutes. An adult ticket costs €3.50 in high season and €2.20 in low season, and a car with driver is around €14.60 in high season.

faq.question: Will prices in Biograd na Moru rise in 2027?
faq.answer: A moderate increase of about 3–6% over 2026 is a reasonable expectation, especially for peak-season accommodation. This is an estimate based on recent trends, and final rates are set by individual owners and hotels.

faq.question: What is the average hotel price in Biograd na Moru?
faq.answer: Three-star hotels average about €85–105 a night and four-star hotels about €125–155. Five-star rooms average near €290–310, and all rates rise sharply in July and August.

quickAnswer: Plan €60–90 per person per day on a budget, €110–170 mid-range, and €250+ for hotels or villas in Biograd na Moru in 2027. Apartments run €70–120 a night in summer, a sit-down dinner €20–30, and the Tkon ferry about €3.50. July and August prices can double.
